pr_title: Allow null object variants to be casted into any Object-derived classes.
pr_body:
<!--
Please target the `master` branch in priority.
PRs can target `3.x` if the same change was done in `master`, or is not relevant there.

Relevant fixes are cherry-picked for stable branches as needed by maintainers.
You can mention in the description if the change is compatible with `3.x`.
-->

Fixes #62658.

I'm not sure if this is the right way to fix this bug, but since any `Object`-derived classes can be null I don't see why a null object cannot be cast into any class.
pr_comments: Wouldn't this make `is_type()` return `true` when `get_validated_object()` fails for other reasons too?

`is_type` will call `get_validated_object` only if the variant is an object. Afterward if the object ID isn't valid in the variant, `get_validated_object` returns null so the variant is basically null in my opinion.

Also in this case it doesn't fail. It returns the object which is a null pointer (i think it's an object with the ID 0).

Although it doesn't literally hold such an object (ID 0), that's an interesting black box POV of ObjectDB :stuck_out_tongue:  

On another look, this seems safe to me for everywhere `is_type` is currently being used :+1:

This doesn't seem fully correct.
```GDScript

func _run() -> void: 
	var n: Node
	test(n)

func test(n: CharacterBody2D):
	print(n)
```
works.

```GDScript

func _run() -> void: 
	var n: Node = Node.new()
	test(n)

func test(n: CharacterBody2D):
	print(n)
```
doesn't work.

It should fail in both cases. Although you get a correct parse error when `n` is RefCounted.

The PR fixes a case where you can't pass a freed Node to method that expects Node, so maybe it's acceptable if it's not perfect.

The same change needs to be done in `case SCRIPT: case GDSCRIPT` just bellow.

@KoBeWi "It should fail in both cases." - actually, no. It works from analyzer standpoint because `CharacterBody2D` extends `Node`, so one can do `var n: Node = CharacterBody2D.new()`. GDScript is not strict in that regard and hopes that you know that `n` is a `CharacterBody2D` when you invoke `test`, but will mark such call as type unsafe.

issue_context.title: `get_node_or_null` returns `[Object:null]` instead of `null`, which breaks when calling a `Node` setter
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.0.alpha.custom_build [602b27c07]

### System information

Arch on 5.18.7-arch1-1

### Issue description

I don't see what the difference is between these values. Therefore, not sure if this is a bug with `get_node_or_null` or `@node_setter`.

```gdscript
func _ready() -> void:
	print(null) # null
	print(get_node_or_null("doesnotexist")) # [Object:null]
```

```gdscript
var node: Node:
	set(value):
		node = value

func _ready() -> void:
	# Invalid type in function '@node_setter' in base 'Node ()'. The Object-derived class of argument 1 (null instance) is not a subclass of the expected argument class.
	node = get_node_or_null("doesnotexist")
```

### Steps to reproduce

1) Run the MRP

### Minimal reproduction project

[test3.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/9034332/test3.zip)

review_comments: Might be worth adding a comment to clarify why this is considered true.
I added a comment there to explain why.
